translation:
  text: '“The believers from the ninth mountain, the desolate one with reptiles and wild beasts that destroy
    people, are like this:


    2. “Those with spots are deacons[a] who served badly, plundered the livelihood of widows and orphans,
    and enriched themselves from the service they had received to perform. If they persist in the same
    desire, they are dead, and there is no hope of life for them. But if they turn back and complete their
    service in purity, they will be able to live.”


    3. “Those covered with scabs are the ones who denied and did not return to their own Lord. Instead,
    they have become barren and desolate. They do not associate with God’s servants but remain alone,
    destroying their own lives.”


    4. “A vine left within a fence and neglected is ruined and overrun by weeds. In time it grows wild
    and is no longer useful to its owner. In the same way, such people have given themselves up as lost;
    by growing wild, they become useless to their own Lord.”


    5. “Repentance is available to them if they are not found to have denied from the heart. But if anyone
    is found to have denied from the heart, I do not know whether that person can live.”


    6. “I do not say this about these present days, so that someone may deny and receive repentance.[b]
    For it is impossible for anyone who now intends to deny their own Lord to be saved. But repentance
    seems to be available to those who denied long ago. So if anyone intends to repent, let them hurry
    before the tower is completed. Otherwise, those women will destroy that person, bringing death.”


    7. “The chipped stones[c] are deceitful people and slanderers. They are the wild beasts you saw on
    the mountain. Just as wild beasts ruin and destroy a person with their venom, so the words of such
    people ruin and destroy a person.”


    8. “They are therefore cut short in their faith because of the conduct they practice. Some, however,
    repented and were saved. The rest who are like them can also be saved if they repent. But if they
    do not repent, they will die through those women whose power they possess.”'
  philosophy: optimal-equivalence
  footnotes:
  - marker: a
    reason: lexical_alternative
    text: Diakonoi is rendered “deacons” in this community-service context. Their assigned care of vulnerable
      people is explicit; the term alone does not settle the structure of a later ordained hierarchy.
  - marker: b
    reason: lexical_alternative
    text: “Receive repentance” keeps the source’s expression and distinction between past denial and present
      intention. The draft retains both its severe impossibility statement and its stated uncertainty,
      rather than harmonizing them. The women are allegorical figures from the vision.
  - marker: c
    reason: lexical_alternative
    text: Koloboi means cut short or mutilated; “chipped stones” retains the stone allegory. The next
      paragraph applies the image to truncated faith; it is not an added description of physical disability.

  text: '“The believers from the ninth mountain, the desolate one with reptiles and wild beasts that destroy
    people, are like this:


    2. “Those with spots are deacons[a] who served badly, plundered the livelihood of widows and orphans,
    and enriched themselves from the service they had received to perform. If they persist in the same
    desire, they are dead, and there is no hope of life for them. But if they turn back and complete their
    service in purity, they will be able to live.”


    3. “Those covered with scabs are the ones who denied and did not return to their own Lord. Instead,
    they have become barren and desolate. They do not associate with God’s servants but remain alone,
    destroying their own lives.”


    4. “A vine left within a fence and neglected is ruined and overrun by weeds. In time it grows wild
    and is no longer useful to its owner. In the same way, such people have given themselves up as lost;
    by growing wild, they become useless to their own Lord.”


    5. “Repentance is available to them if they are not found to have denied from the heart. But if anyone
    is found to have denied from the heart, I do not know whether that person can live.”


    6. “I do not say this about these present days, so that someone may deny and receive repentance.[b]
    For it is impossible for anyone who now intends to deny their own Lord to be saved. But repentance
    seems to be available to those who denied long ago. So if anyone intends to repent, let them hurry
    before the tower is completed. Otherwise, those women will destroy that person, bringing death.”


    7. “The chipped stones[c] are deceitful people and slanderers. They are the wild beasts you saw on
    the mountain. Just as wild beasts ruin and destroy a person with their venom, so the words of such
    people ruin and destroy a person.”


    8. “They are therefore cut short in their faith because of the conduct they practice. Some, however,
    repented and were saved. The rest who are like them can also be saved if they repent. But if they
    do not repent, they will die through those women whose power they possess.”'
